General safety information
Important safety instructions
1.1 Important safety instructions
It is important to install, operate, and do the maintenance correctly on all the equipment. This is
most important for safety related items. For the safety of the User and patients, Elekta
recommends that the User read, understand, and obey:
• All warnings, cautions, and notes in this document and related documents
• All warnings, cautions, and safety markings on the equipment and the accessories of
the equipment
• All safety instructions and information in this document and related documents.
Elekta recommends that:
• All Users obey the precautions in this section
• All Users examine the warnings, cautions, and notes in this document and use them in
their local Work Instructions.
Before the User operates, or do work on the equipment, it is important that they read and
understand the emergency procedures.
1.1.1 Conventions for warnings, cautions, and notes
The conventions give information about the class and the level of the risk in the warnings and
cautions, and the content of notes.
WARNING 1.1
A warning is information about procedures, tasks, or conditions with a risk of fatal or serious
injury, injury, or clinical mistreatment, if you do not obey the instructions.
CAUTION 1.1
A caution is information about procedures, tasks, or conditions with a risk of damage to the
equipment, data, or the environment, if you do not obey the instructions.
Note: A note gives more information about a related text.
1.1.2 Expected service life of the equipment
The expected service life is the length of time that the regular service and repair procedures can
keep the equipment safe to operate.
WARNING 1.2
Do not operate the equipment unless you correctly complete the safety checks, planned
maintenance schedules, and extended life checks. If you ignore this warning, you can cause
fatal injury and damage to the equipment.
The expected service life of this equipment is 15 years of normal use.
The Elekta definition for 'expected service life' is the length of time that the regular service and
repair procedures can keep the equipment safe to operate.
The Elekta definition of 'normal use' is the treatment of 50 patients each day for five days each
week of the year. If the equipment is used more frequently than this, the frequency of the

The level of operation of the equipment can be different to ‘normal use’. This has an effect on the

The system must be maintained throughout its expected service life in compliance with the EMC

For information on the above checks and schedules, contact your local Elekta representative.

General safety information
Safety precautions
1.2 Safety precautions
1.2.1 Safety precautions for the compatibility of the equipment
WARNING 1.3
Do not use parts, accessories, or other equipment, without approval by Elekta of their
compatibility. If you ignore this warning, you can cause fatal injury and damage to the
equipment.
Only operate the equipment with Elekta supplied or approved, compatible equipment or parts.
Accessories, transducers, and cables that are not specified by or do not have the approval of
Elekta can cause an incorrect treatment delivery. They can also have an effect on the performance
of the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), which can increase the emissions or decrease the
immunity of the equipment.
Contact Elekta for information about the compatibility of other equipment or parts.
1.2.2 Safety precautions for the electromagnetic compatibility
The design and manufacture of Elekta products is in compliance with applicable EMC standards.
The intended result of the standards is to minimize the risk of electromagnetic interference by RF
devices. The type of device and the distance to the equipment has an effect on the intensity of
the electromagnetic interference. The equipment includes the linear accelerator and accessories,
the control cabinets, the computers in the control room, and equipment from other
manufacturer.
It is necessary to have special precautions for EMC emissions. Elekta recommends that you obey
these precautions when you use RF devices near the equipment.
• Do not use RF devices unless they are in compliance with international standards for
electromagnetic compatibility, for example, the CE or FCC mark.
• Do not use a two-way emergency radio in the treatment room or the control room.
Only use an emergency radio if there is an emergency.
• Do not use cellular telephones, or other devices with cellular modems near the
equipment. The Instructions for Use contains information on the minimum safe distance
of these devices from the equipment.
• When you use a device that is enabled for wireless operation, it must be a minimum of
10 cm from the equipment.
• Radio-Frequency Identification (RFID) readers, when activated to do a scan of a RFID
tag, must be a minimum of one meter from the equipment.
Note: The RFID systems that Elekta supply use lower power levels. You can safely use these RFID systems
when you obey the procedures in the Instructions for Use for the product.
The system must be installed, put into service, and maintained in compliance with the EMC
information in the Instructions for Use.
Contact Elekta for information about the compatibility of parts and equipment.

Safety precautions
WARNING 1.4
Do not put portable or mobile radio frequency (RF) communication devices near to the
equipment. The emissions from such RF devices can be more than the EMC standards, and can
have unwanted effects on the equipment operation. If you ignore this warning, the RF
emissions can cause the equipment to have a malfunction. A malfunction can cause fatal injury,
clinical mistreatment, or damage to the equipment.
WARNING 1.5
Do not use accessories, transducers, and cables that are not specified by Elekta. They can have
an effect on the EMC performance, which can increase EMC emissions or decrease the
immunity to RF interference of the equipment. If you ignore this warning, incorrect radiation
delivery and other malfunctions can occur, which can cause fatal injury or clinical mistreatment.
1.2.3 Safety precautions for operation of the equipment
WARNING 1.6
Do not operate the equipment unless the QA checks are satisfactorily completed. If you ignore
this warning, you can cause fatal injury and damage to the equipment.
WARNING 1.7
Do not operate the equipment if it is damaged, defective, or incorrectly calibrated. If you ignore
this warning, you can cause fatal injury and damage to the equipment.
Only operate the equipment if you are a qualified person with the applicable authority. Such
operation must apply best practice for clinical treatment and obey the laws and regulations in the
jurisdiction in which the equipment is installed.
Before you operate the equipment, make sure that:
• There are no defective parts.
• The equipment calibration is correct.
• The applicable QA checks are satisfactorily completed.
• The user routine checks are satisfactorily completed.
• The planned maintenance schedule is completed satisfactorily.
For information on the user routine checks and the planned maintenance schedule, see the
applicable section of the Instructions for Use.
It is the responsibility of the User to set up a QA program that gives safe and satisfactory system
operation.
1.2.4 Safety precaution for Service Tools and lifting equipment
WARNING 1.8
Do not use defective or damaged lifting equipment. If you ignore this warning, you can cause
fatal injury and damage to the equipment.

WARNING 1.9
Do not use incorrectly calibrated or defective Service Tools. If you ignore this warning, you can
cause injury and damage to the equipment.
Before you use the Service Tool or lifting equipment, make sure that:
• There are no defective or damaged parts
• The calibration of the Service Tool is correct
• The applicable calibration certificate is valid
• The lifting equipment gives the maximum Safe Working Load (SWL).
For information on the maintenance and calibration schedules of the Service Tool, see the
Instructions for Use and Calibration Certificate for the tool.
1.2.5 Safety precaution for work with electrical and mechanical parts
WARNING 1.10
Do not connect any electrical power supply before the ground earth connections are secure.
There is a risk of high leakage current. If you ignore this warning, you can cause fatal injury.
WARNING 1.11
Do not remove the cables or the covers, or operate the equipment without the covers. If you
ignore this warning, you can cause fatal injury
The covers on the equipment prevent access to high voltage parts and parts that move. If you
remove the covers, there is a risk of high voltage shock or injury from parts that move.
Only remove the covers if you are an Elekta approved person with the correct authority and you
obey the applicable safety procedures.
1.2.6 Safety precaution for work with safety devices during service
operation
WARNING 1.12
Do not remove, change, or override the safety switches, interlocks, and other safety devices. If
you ignore this warning, you can cause fatal injury or clinical mistreatment.
The procedures in this document can tell you to remove, change, or override the safety switches,
interlocks, or other safety devices during repair or maintenance work. When the work is
completed, make all the safety devices active again, and do a test of them.
1.2.7 Safety precaution for work on BLDs with UV lighting
WARNING 1.13
Do not look into the ultraviolet lighting of the BLD without protective glasses. If you ignore this
warning, you can cause serious injury.

The covers and screens of the BLD prevent an injury to your eyes from the ultraviolet lighting.
Before you remove the covers or screens of the BLD, switch off the linear accelerator, or use
protective glasses. Protective glasses must have the UV-A specification OD 6+ @ 190 - 532 Nm.
If there is damage to the covers or screen of the BLD, switch off the linear accelerator and contact
the Elekta representative.
1.2.8 Safety precaution for work with lasers
WARNING 1.14
Do not look into the laser beams because they can cause damage to your eyes. If you ignore
this warning, you can cause serious injury.
Elekta systems use the laser beams to help set up patients in the correct position for treatment.
During your work in the treatment room, make sure that you do not look into the laser beams.
1.2.9 Safety precautions for work with display screen equipment
WARNING 1.15
Do not use the display screen equipment for long periods of time. If you ignore this warning,
you can cause injury.
When you use the display screen equipment (DSE), obey the applicable Health and Safety
regulations and procedures in the jurisdiction where you do the work.
1.2.10 Safety precautions for cleaning and disinfection
WARNING 1.16
Do not clean the equipment, or use a disinfectant spray when the equipment is connected to
the electrical supply. If you ignore this warning, you can cause fatal injury.
WARNING 1.17
Do not use a spray that is explosive or flammable. If you ignore this warning, you can cause
fatal injury and damage to the equipment.
CAUTION 1.2
Do not let water and other liquids go into the equipment. If you ignore this caution, you can
cause damage to the equipment.
CAUTION 1.3
Do not use a spray to clean the medical equipment room. If you ignore this caution, you can
cause damage to the equipment.
At regular intervals, it is necessary to clean the equipment and equipment room with
disinfectants. Elekta recommends that the procedures to clean the equipment and the equipment
room obey the applicable laws and regulations of the jurisdiction where the equipment is
installed.

General safety information
Safety precautions
1.2.11 Safety precautions for work with high temperatures on the BLD
covers
During normal operation, the maximum temperatures of the accessory ring and BLD outer covers
can increase to 45° C. Make sure that you do not touch the outer covers or the accessory ring for
more than 1 minute.
1.2.12 Safety precaution for the installation of accessories on the BLD
WARNING 1.18
Do not touch the connector found in the accessory ring on the BLD. If you ignore this warning,
you can cause injury.
When you install an accessory, for example, a shadow tray, electron applicator, or front pointer,
do not touch the pins in the connector. The pins have a low electrical current, which can give an
electric shock when you touch them.
1.2.13 Safety precautions for work with heavy parts
The safety precautions for work with heavy parts are the necessary safety precautions to know to
prevent injury.
WARNING 1.19
Do not lift or move heavy parts unless you obey the applicable Health and Safety regulations
and procedures. If you ignore this warning, you can cause serious injury.
1.2.14 Safety precautions during work on the BLD
When you do work on the BLD, make sure that you obey the following safety precautions:
WARNING 1.20
Do not do work on the inner parts of the beam limiting device while the electrical supply is
connected. There is a risk of high voltage electric shock. If you ignore this warning, you can
cause fatal injury.
WARNING 1.21
Do not do work on the beam limiting device unless the gantry is at 0° or 180°. Gravity can cause
the leaves, diaphragms, and dynamic leaf guides to move. If you ignore this warning, you can
cause fatal injury.
WARNING 1.22
Do not touch the hot LED field light projector, or the heat sink, immediately after operation. If
you ignore this warning, you can cause serious injury.

General safety information
Safety precautions
1.2.15 Safety precaution for the removal of parts from the radiation head
WARNING 1.23
Do not touch the flight tube, bending magnet, or other parts near to them until a check for
induced radioactivity is completed. Excessive exposure to radioactivity is dangerous. If you
ignore this warning, you can cause serious injury.
After the operation of the linear accelerator at high energy, the parts in the radiation head can
become radioactive and a radiation hazard. Before you do work on, or remove parts from the
radiation head, use a calibrated radiation detector to measure the level of induced radioactivity.
Use the applicable safety procedures when you remove radioactive parts and material. The
maximum dose rate for the safe removal of radioactive parts and material is 50 µSv/hr
(microsievert per hour). Do not remove the radioactive parts and material from the treatment
room before they are correctly prepared for safe removal.
1.2.16 Safety precautions for maintenance, modification, and
decommissioning
WARNING 1.24
Do not do work, or make modifications to the equipment without the correct training and
authority. If you ignore this warning, you can cause fatal injury, clinical mistreatment, and
damage to the equipment.
Only do work on, or make modifications to, the equipment if you are an Elekta approved person
with the applicable authority. Such work must use best practice and obey the laws and
regulations in the jurisdiction in which the equipment is installed.
Modifications or work that does not have approval by Elekta, and is not done by an Elekta
approved person with the correct authority, can cause:
• Fatal injury
• Incorrect radiation delivery
• Malfunction of the equipment
• Damage to the equipment
• The warranty to be canceled.
1.2.17 Safety precautions for work in areas of induced radioactivity
The safety precautions for work in areas of induced radioactivity are the precautions to prevent
an excessive exposure to, and serious injury from, induced radioactivity.
When you operate or do work on the equipment, Elekta recommends that you use the applicable
radiation protection functions, devices, systems, procedures, and accessories. Always obey the
applicable laws and regulations for induced radioactivity for the jurisdiction in which the
equipment is installed.
The safety precautions are applicable to:

Safety precautions

1.2.17.1 Safety precautions for the measurement of induced radioactivity
The safety precautions for the measurement of induced radioactivity are the necessary safety
precautions to know to prevent excessive exposure to radioactivity, which can cause serious
injury or damage to the environment.
Always use two radiation detectors to measure the level of induced radioactivity. Only use
radiation detectors that have an applicable calibration certificate. The period of time since the
last calibration date must be less than 12 months. Do not use the radiation detectors if the period
of time since the last calibration date is more than 12 months.
WARNING 1.25
Do not move radioactive material (by air, sea, or land) unless you obey the applicable laws and
regulations for induced radioactivity and disposal of radioactive material of the jurisdictions
through which the movement occurs. If you ignore this warning, you can cause serious injury
and damage to the environment.
1.2.17.2 Safety precautions for handling parts with induced radioactivity
The handling of parts with induced radioactivity must comply with the laws and regulations of the
jurisdiction in which the equipment is installed. The safe levels of radiation applicable in the UK
do not apply in all jurisdictions. The permitted level of radioactivity must always be as low as
reasonably achievable (ALARA). This level may vary depending on local rules, therefore the safe
working levels from the applicable local rules must be considered as the acceptable working limit.
If there are no safe levels available for a jurisdiction, use the UK value as a guideline, which is a
maximum of 150 cps at the surface for a maximum duration of 72 minutes. The following table
shows the conversion from this value to other units.

WARNING 1.26
Do not use the equipment in rooms that contain explosive or flammable gases. If you ignore
this warning, you can cause fatal injury and damage to the equipment.

High levels of oxygen, and some anesthetic gases and disinfectant sprays, can make an explosive
or flammable environment in the room.
1.3.2 Recommendations for emergency procedures
Before you use the equipment, Elekta recommends that you know all the local emergency
procedures and the locations of all the emergency switches.
The Elekta equipment includes:
• The STOP MOTORS buttons on the handheld controllers and user interface panels in the
treatment room, and FKP in the control room.
When you press these buttons, it disconnects the electrical supply from the motors,
stops all movements of the equipment, and stops kV and MV radiation.
• The EMERGENCY POWER OFF buttons in the treatment room, control area, and areas
near the equipment.
When you operate these buttons, it disconnects the electrical supply to the linear
accelerator. The buttons disconnect the electrical supply from many electrical circuits,
but not from all the circuits.

2.3 Regulatory requirements for equipment use
2.3.1 Precautions for work with electrostatic discharge sensitive devices
CAUTION 2.1
Do not touch the PCBs and other electronic parts unless you wear a grounded antistatic wrist
strap. If you ignore this caution, you can cause damage to the equipment.
CAUTION 2.2
Do not touch the parts identified with the ESD caution label. Always obey the ESD precautions
during work on these parts. If you ignore this caution, you can cause damage to the equipment.
Semiconductor devices, integrated circuits, and the parts that contain them, are ESD sensitive
devices. These devices are electrostatic discharge sensitive (ESDS) devices. ESD can cause damage
to these devices and cause them to have a malfunction immediately or some time after the
electrostatic discharge. To prevent the ESD damage to these devices, always wear a grounded
antistatic wrist strap, and obey the applicable ESD precautions and procedures.
Elekta recommends that all users receive the training about ESD. The training must include the
ESD caution label and these ESD precautions.

Introduction
Document scope
3.1 Document scope
The Service User Guide helps service engineers in the safe and correct servicing and maintenance
of the Integrity™ software in Service Mode, and the Consolidated Computing Platform (CCP).
Integrity™ is the interface and control software for the Elekta range of medical linear accelerators.
The target audience of this document is qualified service engineers. These can be engineers
employed directly by Elekta, qualified representatives of Elekta or qualified representatives of the
Elekta customer.
This manual provides service user information on:
• The necessary safety precautions
• Product description of the CCP
• Getting starting in Service Mode
• Using the Integrity software
• Using the CCP
• Troubleshooting the CCP
• Corrective maintenance of the CCP
This document contains a General safety and Regulatory Information chapter, which you must
read before using the rest of the document.
If you discover any mistakes in this document, or identify areas for improvement, raise a CLM
(customer life cycle management) case and assign it to the relevant queue.
3.2 Accompanying documentation
The customer documentation set for this equipment includes these documents:
• Elekta Medical Linear Accelerator Instructions for Use
• Elekta Medical Linear Accelerator Clinical Technical Reference
• IEC 60976 / 60977 Performance Values
• Elekta Medical Linear Accelerator Site and Type Tests
• IT Risk Management
• iViewGT™ Instructions for Use (not used in all models)
• XVI Instructions for Use (not used in all models)
• Relevant couchtop Instructions for Use (HexaPOD™, or iBEAM® evo).
Service and installation documentation are only available on request.
Note: 'Accompanying documentation' are the customer documents that must be available for the
installed linear accelerator configuration at the time of handover.
Site and Type Tests
The Site and Type Tests Manual for the Elekta Medical Linear Accelerator is mandatory for
compliance with IEC 60601-2-1 Clause 201.10.
The standard contains the limits for safe operation of the equipment. If the conditions of
operation go through these limits, the safety design of the equipment makes sure that the
interlocks prevent, interrupt, or terminate the irradiation.
This document gives you the necessary information on:

Description of Integrity™ and available delivery techniques
4.1 Description of Integrity™ and available delivery techniques
Integrity™ is the program that runs on the consolidated computing platform (CCP) and controls
the linear accelerator. All the clinical functions are available through the Integrity™ user interface.
The Clinical User can use a number of delivery techniques with Integrity™. These are available in
all X-ray energies and include electron treatment. Linear accelerators with Agility™ are supplied
with High Dose Rate mode and FFF energies. Software licenses are necessary for these delivery
techniques:
• PreciseBEAM™ Segmental
• PreciseBEAM™ Dynamic
• PreciseBEAM™ Dynamic Arc
• PreciseBEAM™ VMAT
• HDRE.
You can use CVDR for Dynamic, Dynamic Arc, and VMAT.
There is an interdigitation function of the leaves for the MLCi2™ and Agility™.
Note: When you use new or unusual treatment methods, it is the responsibility of the user to make sure
that the linear accelerator can deliver the treatment.
4.2 Description and layout of the linear accelerator
The linear accelerator, treatment table, and imaging hardware are primarily installed in the
treatment room. The control systems are in the control room and many of the mechanical parts
of the linear accelerator are in the equipment room.

4.4.1 Description of the consolidated computing platform (CCP) system
The consolidated computing platform (CCP) system is a treatment control system. A treatment
control system includes a treatment control cabinet (CCP cabinet), a keyboard, monitors, a
mouse, and the Integrity™ software. Integrity™ is the program that controls the linear accelerator.
All the clinical functions are available through the Integrity™ user interface. Integrity™ and
IntelliMax Agent run as virtual machines (VM) and are supported by an Enterprise Server.
The CCP system also includes a CCP Management Computer (R&V system), and a treatment room
monitor (TRM) computer.
The CCP cabinet includes:
• RT Computer
• Network attached storage (NAS)
• Ethernet switch
• Network management and security (includes firewall solution)
• Enterprise server
• UPS.

The CCP Management Computer (CCPMC) is located in the control room. It drives three or four

the CCPMC responds to this command and the Integrity primary monitor goes blank.

4.4.4 Description of the remote viewer application (RVA) configuration
The remote viewer application (RVA) allows you to view the screen of another remote device on
the local computer and gives you control of the keyboard and mouse of the remote device that
you are controlling.
There are three different classification of monitors as follows:
• RVA monitor. A monitor that can be controlled by the RVA. In this mode, the RVA
application is set to Always on Top. Another application is not allowed to appear in
front of the RVA. If another Windows application tries to appear underneath the RVA,
preference is given to the main Windows display (if not used by the RVA) or to the
lowest numbered non-RVA monitor.
• Hideable-RVA monitor. An RVA monitor can be switched to be hidden, if it has been
configured with this option. When hidden, the monitor behaves like a non-RVA monitor.
• Non-RVA monitor. A non-RVA monitor cannot be controlled by the RVA. It can only be
controlled by the local host computer on which you are running the RVA application.
Rules for configuring the RVA on the CCP management computer:
• There must always be at least one non-RVA monitor so that you can access the CCP
management panel. The non-RVA monitor is also the CCP management main display.
• The R&V channel must be on a non-RVA monitor.
• For a horizontal layout of the monitors, the RVA monitors must always be next to each
other and cannot have a non-RVA monitor between them.
• For a grid layout of monitors, the RVA can occupy a single monitor or two monitors. If it
occupies two monitors then the monitors must be in the same row, or the same
column.
• You cannot configure the Integrity primary monitor as hidden as it is a regulatory
requirement for it to always be visible. The Terminal Services Configuration Editor
application stops you from making this monitor hidden.
The remote viewer application (RVA) is installed on the CCP management computer (in the
control room) and the TRM computer (in the equipment room). The RVA allows you to display
and control different applications and channels on different monitors. For example, you can
display MOSAIQ Sequencer or Integrity on the monitors in the treatment room or in the control
room. You can also select which system to display and on which monitor. This is configured by the
Service representative in accordance with customer requirements. Customers should not attempt
to configure this for themselves.
For a horizontal layout of monitors, the RVA numbers all the monitors from left to right, whether
the monitors are used by the RVA or not.
In case of a grid layout, if the left coordinates are the same, then RVA numbers the monitors from
top to bottom. This order can be different to how Windows numbers the monitors.
Note: The numbering used by Windows is not based on physical position of the monitors and can vary
from one computer to another. The CCP uses its own numbering system based on the logical
positions of the monitors
The CCP management computer in the control room can control between two and four monitors.
The TRM computer in the equipment room can control between two and three monitors. The
exact configuration depends on customer requirements.

4.4.7 Description of the Network-attached storage (NAS)
The Network-attached storage (NAS) is a storage device connected to the CCP internal network.
The CCP uses a QNAP NAS for this purpose. NAS replaces the separate NSS backup server and is
accessible by treatment devices for all data storage purposes.
The NAS has two LAN ports which are configured during the initial installation:
• LAN 1 is connected to the management subnet via the network switch. This allows
management of the NAS configuration using a web interface.
• LAN 2 of the NAS is connected to the Treatment subnet via the network switch. This
allows access from all connected devices.
4.4.8 Description of a virtual machine (VM)
A virtual machine (VM) is an emulation of a computer system. Virtual machines provide the same
functionality as physical computers. An Enterprise server is a server which provides multiple
virtual machines on a single piece of hardware. This means you can save the costs and the space
associated with multiple hardware servers. The hardware for the Enterprise server must be
extensive enough to emulate the hardware resources of multiple servers, and it needs special
management software to manage these resources. The software is called VMware.
The virtual machine provides the functionality needed to run entire operating systems. A
hypervisor manages the hardware, allowing for multiple environments which are isolated from
one another, but exist on the same physical machine.

4.4.9 Description of the IntelliMax virtual machine
IntelliMax is a suite of services which provide remote support and proactive maintenance for the
configured treatment devices. IntelliMax Connect provides remote support. It also utilizes VNC
technology.
The IntelliMax Agent is installed on the IntelliMax VM. This IntelliMax agent acts as a conduit for
the remote services within the hospital. Its tasks include:
• Controlling the IntelliMax Connect traffic.
• Maintaining real time data collection from all the devices.
• Allowing software to be distributed electronically.
The collected data is sent to the remote IntelliMax server (IntelliMax Enterprise), where the data
is analysed. Notifications can be sent to engineers to inform them of existing or pending failures.
4.4.10 Description of the real-time controller (RTC)
The real-time controller (RTC) has a very similar configuration to the existing real time controller
in the treatment control system. This is a customized industrial computer with the following
components:
• ATX power supply and motherboard
• Linac interface card
• 1553 serial link card
• Frame grabber card
• ROOM card – for driving BMDM
• CAN and LAN interface cards.
4.4.10.1 EMC shielding for the consolidated computing platform (CCP)
Medical device regulations require a compliant level of EMC shielding.
The real-time computer (RTC) is an extension of the medical device and is designed to comply
with these regulations as well as being contained within a shielded cabinet. The commercial
computing hardware is housed below the RTC with a high level of shielding to make it compatible
with medical requirements.

4.4.11 Description of the Enterprise server
The Enterprise Server (ES) runs the VMware ESXi hypervisor. The ES has a similar function to the
existing non-real-time computer (NRT) in the control system.
The ES has the following components:
• A processor
• 32 GB RAM (minimum)
• 2 x HDD configured with RAID 1 (hot swappable)
• Dual 500W PSU (hot swappable).
The ES hosts two virtual machines, one for the Integrity software and the other for IntelliMax
Agent. It is possible to configure it to be the host of more virtual machines (VM).
The ES has four ethernet ports to connect the four LAN subnets:
• Port NIC-0 is connected to the management subnet via the network switch. The ESXi
operating system uses this port.
• Port NIC-1 is connected to the NRT (non-real-time) subnet via the network switch,
which is used internally by the Integrity virtual machine.
• Port NIC-2 is connected to the RT (real-time) subnet via the network switch, which is
used internally by the Integrity VM.
• Port NIC-3 is connected to the remote monitoring subnet via the network switch, which
is used internally by the IntelliMax Agent VM.
There is an additional dedicated LAN port for iLO (Integrated Lights Out). iLO is used to monitor
the system health of the server. iLO is connected directly to the switch and has a static IP address
on the management network (192.168.240.250). You can access the iLO through the CCP
management computer (CCPMC). Use the login details on the tag in front of the server.

4.4.12 Description of the uninterruptible power supply
The Consolidated Computing platform (CCP) contains an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) that
supplies auxiliary power to the CCP, Integrity computer and the R&V system (MOSAIQ™). If there
is a power failure, a fully charged UPS supplies power to the CCP and its devices for approximately
five minutes. This gives you sufficient time to save the treatment data and correctly shut down
the system.
Note: Elekta recommends that all network components are supplied via a UPS.
The UPS changes to battery backup immediately after a power failure. After 10 seconds, the
treatment control system starts the shutdown procedure. If the power is restored in less than
10 seconds, the UPS changes back to mains operation and the shutdown procedure is not started.
This operation of the UPS prevents interruptions in the operation of the treatment control system
during short power failures.
When the UPS is in battery operation mode, there is an audible alarm at 10 second intervals. This
alarm continues until power is restored or the UPS is drained of power.
If the power cable connection from the treatment control cabinet to the UPS is damaged, or the
UPS is not in operation, the UPS will not supply power. If a fault with the communication
connection to the UPS occurs, a message appears in the status bar. The UPS unavailable icon also
appears in the system status indicator.
Figure 4.17 Failure of the connection to the UPS
If there is a power failure, the power to the Beam MU Display Module (BMDM) will continue for a
minimum of 20 minutes. This will give you sufficient time to record the displayed BEAM MU.
Note: If the UPS fails to change to battery backup or the UPS loses power before and during the power
failure, contact your local Elekta representative.
4.4.13 Description of the Network Management and Security Device
The Network Management and Security (NMaS) device provides firewall protection from external
computer data networks to the local area networks within the CCP. NMaS uses a stand-alone,
network security firewall/gateway device. It interconnects the treatment subnet, Service LAN
subnet, IntelliMax subnet and the hospital LAN. It implements policies to control the exchange of
data traffic between pre-defined subnets.
The NMaS is implemented using a Juniper SRX-300 firewall. It has 4 connected interfaces:
• Port 0 is connected to the hospital network.
• Port 1 is connected to the treatment network.

4.4.18 Description of the keyboard and mouse devices
The linear accelerator has local keyboard and mouse devices in the control room for the primary
terminal. You can have a secondary terminal in the treatment room, which has a keyboard,
monitor, and mouse.This secondary terminal has the same functions as the primary terminal in
the control room. When one terminal is in operation, there is an interval of one second before
you can use the other terminal.
Press the SCROLL LOCK key on the primary keyboard in the control room to lock the secondary
terminal. Press the SCROLL LOCK key again to unlock the secondary terminal access.
Note: After you use the secondary terminal in the treatment room, make sure that the settings are
correct. Make sure that the settings have no third-party adjustments (with or without authority).
Note: All instructions in this manual for the keyboard and mouse are written for a standard English (UK)
keyboard and mouse.
4.4.19 Description of the Backup and Restore Tool
The Backup and Restore Tool (BURT) is an application installed on the CCP Management
Computer (CCPMC).
BURT allows you to manage the backup and restore of the Integrity™ and IntelliMax virtual
machines with the following functions:
• Create a backup of a virtual machine.
• Restore a virtual machine from a backup.
• Delete or upload a backup.

4.6 Description of the treatment room equipment
4.6.1 Description of the electron applicator types
The electron applicators help deliver constant, high definition, treatment fields of the necessary
dimensions. There are five types of electron applicator:
• Square
• Rectangular, which includes the short SSD electron applicator for arc therapy
• Circular
• Null applicator
• HDRE.
A blank bottom unit is available for special customizations.
Each electron applicator attaches to the BLD with a hook and latch system.
The BLD leaves are automatically set to the best position for the selected electron applicator and
energy. The default auto-tracking settings for each energy and electron applicator can be
changed, in Service Mode, to the best position for the BLD. Contact your Elekta representative to
change this setting.
Document ID: 1548888_03 Elekta Medical Linear Accelerator

Page 66 © Elekta Group 2021. All rights reserved.

Product description
Description of the treatment room equipment
Note: The auto-tracking default values are in compliance with IEC 60601-2-1 clause 201.10.1.2.103.2.2.
If the values of the autotracking settings are greater than the default values supplied by Elekta,
the electron applicator must be tested. If necessary, contact your service representative.
Note: If the autotracking settings are changed, this will change the dose distribution. Any change in the
settings must be evaluated by Medical Physics Expert (MPE) before clinical use.
You must only use the short SSD electron applicator for electron arc therapy. Elekta recommends
that you keep a unique combination of applicator type, size and end frame code for the short SSD
electron applicator.
The distance from the end of the electron applicator to the target is usually 95 cm. But for arc
therapy with the short SSD electron applicator, it is 82 cm.
Contact your local Elekta representative for the current part number.
4.6.2 Description of the end frames of the square and rectangular
electron applicators
Elekta supplies the end frames of standard sizes at the same nominal size as the electron
applicator. These have an end frame code of 1.
You can attach and remove the end frames. It is possible to make irregular end frame shapes from
the applicable shielding block material. The irregular end frame shapes can be the same shape as
the treatment area. These must have an end frame code of 2 to 14. You can use a maximum of 14
end frame codes for each electron applicator.
You can replace the standard frame in the slide rails at the end of the electron applicator with the
irregular end frame. The end frame must have a height of 9.8 mm to 10.0 mm (nominal).
4.6.3 Description of the touchguard of the square and rectangular
electron applicators
The square and rectangular electron applicators have spring-loaded pillars which hold the end
frames. When the end frames apply pressure to the pillars, the springs compress and operate as a
touchguard. If the springs compress by more than 3 mm to 5 mm (nominal), they activate a
microswitch. The microswitch stops all motor drives to the linear accelerator and treatment table,
and the system terminates the radiation delivery.
4.6.4 Description of the circular electron applicators
The circular electron applicators have four end tubes made of stainless steel. Each end tube has
an identification code. The end tubes are available in a range of inner diameters: 2 cm, 3 cm,
4 cm, and 5 cm. The circular electron applicators are identified with 2, 3, 4, and 5, which is their
size in centimeters.

4.6.5 Description of the touchguard of the circular electron applicators
The interchangeable end tubes each fit into a spring-loaded retainer mechanism. The mechanism
activates the touchguard microswitch when the end tube compresses the spring-loaded retainer
mechanism by 8 mm to 10 mm (nominal).
4.6.6 Description of the touchguard system of the linear accelerator
The linear accelerator has a touchguard system that activates if there is a collision between a
touchguard and an object. Make sure that the touchguards attach correctly at all times.
Note: Elekta recommends that you do not remove a touchguard unless told to in an Elekta manual.
If a touchguard activates, you must find the cause and remove it. No movements can occur when
a touchguard activates. To override this, you must press the TOUCHGUARD button on the HHC or
the TOUCHGUARD OVERRIDE button on one of the user interface modules of the treatment table.
WARNING 4.1
Do not continue, after you operate the TOUCHGUARD OVERRIDE button, unless all subsequent
movements are away from the collision condition. If you ignore this warning, you can cause
serious injury.
Note: The system software does not include functions for protection against collisions.
4.6.7 Handheld controller
The type of handheld controller (HHC) depends on the configuration of the linear accelerator.
The handheld controller (HHC) lets you control:
• Mechanical functions of the system, for example, gantry rotation, collimator rotation,
treatment table movement, and field settings.
• Treatment room monitor (TRM) page displays, treatment room lights, optical distance
indicator (ODI), and laser light settings.
• Linear accelerator and table automatic setup (ASU).
• Remote automatic table movements (RATM).

4.10 Description of the uninterruptible power supply
The Consolidated Computing platform (CCP) contains an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) that
supplies auxiliary power to the CCP, Integrity computer and the R&V system (MOSAIQ™). If there
is a power failure, a fully charged UPS supplies power to the CCP and its devices for approximately
five minutes. This gives you sufficient time to save the treatment data and correctly shut down
the system.
Note: Elekta recommends that all network components are supplied via a UPS.
The UPS changes to battery backup immediately after a power failure. After 10 seconds, the
treatment control system starts the shutdown procedure. If the power is restored in less than
10 seconds, the UPS changes back to mains operation and the shutdown procedure is not started.
This operation of the UPS prevents interruptions in the operation of the treatment control system
during short power failures.

Product description
Description of the uninterruptible power supply
When the UPS is in battery operation mode, there is an audible alarm at 10 second intervals. This
alarm continues until power is restored or the UPS is drained of power.
If the power cable connection from the treatment control cabinet to the UPS is damaged, or the
UPS is not in operation, the UPS will not supply power. If a fault with the communication
connection to the UPS occurs, a message appears in the status bar. The UPS unavailable icon also
appears in the system status indicator.
Figure 4.33 Failure of the connection to the UPS
If there is a power failure, the power to the Beam MU Display Module (BMDM) will continue for a
minimum of 20 minutes. This will give you sufficient time to record the displayed BEAM MU.
Note: If the UPS fails to change to battery backup or the UPS loses power before and during the power
failure, contact your local Elekta representative.
4.10.1 Description of operation where there is a failure of the electrical
power supply
If there is a failure of the electrical power supply, or if you press the Emergency Power Off button,
the UPS starts. After 10 seconds, Integrity™ switches off the system.
If the power failure occurs when radiation is on, the treatment terminates immediately and the
Power Supply dialog box opens. This acknowledges the power failure and tells you that Integrity™
will not complete the radiation delivery. The Linac Record records data for the delivered radiation
until the time of the power failure.
You have 5 minutes to manually record other displayed data, for example with the PRINT SCREEN
key, and switch off the system correctly. If you do not switch off the system in less than 5 minutes,
the system will shut down automatically.
If you were in Receive External Prescription when a power failure occurs, save the treatment
data on the R&V system. If you do not save the treatment data, see the documentation for the
R&V system for more information.
Note: You cannot continue to deliver a treatment field when there is a failure of the electrical power
supply. This is applicable for all modes of treatment.
4.10.2 Description of operation when there is a power failure at the
control cabinet
If a power failure occurs in Receive External Prescription during non-dynamic delivery, the field
continues until normal termination. Integrity™ shows the Power Supply dialog box, which
acknowledges that a power failure occurred (see Figure 4.34).
Note: The connection to the UPS must be configured for the dialog box to be shown.

The Precise Treatment Table™ can be moved manually, or by using the controls for motorized
movements.
The treatment table has two user interface modules. Their controls are a mirror of each other.
You can:
• Release the brakes.
• Do motorized movements or manual movements.
• Override the touchguard inhibits.
• Stop the movements if there is an emergency.
• Use the emergency down drive procedure to lower the treatment table if there is a
failure of the electrical power supply.
When the lamp in a brake release button is on, you can use motorized movements to move the
treatment table, but cannot do manual movements. You can move the treatment table in the
direction of the arrows on the brake release button.
The lamp goes off when you press a brake release button. You can then move the treatment table
manually in the direction of the arrows.
Column rotation is not a motorized movement.

4.12.4 Description of the ENABLE bar and thumbwheels
The ENABLE bar and thumbwheels control the motorized movement of the treatment table. The
treatment table moves in the direction of the thumbwheel operation. When the thumbwheel and
the ENABLE bar are released, movement of the treatment table stops.
You can control the speed of the treatment table movement by the pressure applied to the
thumbwheel.
4.12.5 BRAKE RELEASE buttons
There are three brake release buttons on the standard configuration of the user interface
modules:
• COLUMN BRAKE: column rotation brake
• ISO-ROTATION BRAKE: isocentric rotation brake
• LATERAL/LONGITUDINAL BRAKE: lateral/longitudinal movement brake.
Note: The column and lateral brakes must not be in the released state at the same time. If both brakes
are released, whilst you make one type of movement, you can accidentally move the other part of
the treatment table.
If the lamp in a BRAKE RELEASE button is on, you can move the treatment table in that axis using
motorized movement. You cannot move it manually in that axis. Movement in the other axes is
not affected.
If the lamp in a BRAKE RELEASE button is off, you can move the treatment table in that axis
manually. You cannot move it using motorized movements. Movement in the other axes is not
affected.

When the treatment table is not fully at 0°, the TRM can continue to show a Column Rotation
value of 0°. If this occurs, the user will continue to think that the column rotation is in the same
position. When the user rotates the column towards or away from 0° and applies the column

4.12.6 Description of the STOP MOTORS button
The red STOP MOTOR button extends from the side of the user interface modules. When you
press a STOP MOTORS button on the user interface modules, it immediately stops all the
motorized movements and locks into position. It does not remove the power supply to the linear
accelerator. To reactivate the motors, turn the button to release it.
4.12.7 Description of the emergency down drive procedure
The emergency down drive procedure lowers the treatment table to let you remove a patient
safely after an electrical supply failure.
Removal of the power supply shuts down all functions except the emergency down drive.
Before you can invoke the emergency down drive procedure, you must first press one of the
EMERGENCY STOP buttons in the treatment room or control room.
You must not move the treatment table in the upwards direction if there is a power supply failure.
The uninterruptible power supply (UPS) sounds an alarm, warning you not to do this. The UPS
supplies power for the emergency down drive operation for approximately five minutes after the
electrical supply stops.
4.12.8 Description of the protective device in the height drive mechanism
The height drive mechanism has a protective safety device to prevent the treatment table from
sudden collapse. You must not use the height drive after a malfunction activates this protective
device, as this may result in damage to the equipment.
If a malfunction activates the protective device, do not use the treatment table and do not try to
repair the height drive mechanism or the activated protective device. Contact your Elekta
representative to get an Elekta approved person to install a replacement safety device.
4.12.9 Permitted loads for the treatment table
WARNING 4.4
Do not put more than the maximum permitted load on the treatment table. The load must be
distributed equally along the length of the treatment table. If you ignore this warning, you can
cause serious injury and damage to the equipment.
The maximum permitted patient load distribution for the treatment table is 250 kg.

motorized movement. You cannot move it manually in that axis. Movement in the other axes is
not affected.
If the lamp in a BRAKE button is off, you can move the treatment table in that axis manually. You
cannot move it using motorized movements. Movement in the other axes is not affected.
WARNING 4.5
Do not apply the column brake until the column rotation is at 0° and the indent mechanism
engages. If you apply the column brake, and the treatment table is not fully at 0°, you can
accidentally move the treatment table between treatment fields. If you ignore this warning,
you can cause clinical mistreatment.
When the treatment table is not fully at 0°, the TRM can continue to show a Column Rotation
value of 0°. If this occurs, the user will continue to think that the column rotation is in the same
position. When the user rotates the column towards or away from 0° and applies the column
brake, you get an audible indication when the Column Rotation value is within ±5° and not fully
engaged at 0°. The audible indication stops when the column rotation is fully at 0° or greater than
±5°.

5.1 System administrator tasks
5.1.1 Description of the system user access
The system administrator sets up the system users in Clinical Mode. When the system
administrator adds a new user, they set up the user account for Service Mode or Clinical Mode.
When the user types their user name and password on the Logon dialog box, the applicable
window appears.
If it is necessary for a Service User to use the administrator functions in Clinical Mode, they must
have a different user name and password for Clinical Mode.
The system administrator sets the user permissions for each user for some of the functions in the
treatment control system. If a user selects a function, but they do not have the correct user
permission, a dialog box appears. The dialog box tells the user that they do not have the correct
user permission.
5.1.2 Description of the setup of the Elekta Service Users
Elekta personnel each get a user name that is their unique identifier. The Product Supply Center
sends a new password at intervals of three months to the Business Units. The System
Administrator can also set up Elekta personnel as a user. But, they must always log on with their
Elekta user name and password to make sure that the correct information is in the log files.
Elekta Service Users automatically have all user permissions, and can use all the Extended Service
functions. The Elekta Service User can also use the Extended Service functions when the
customer does not have this licensed option.
5.1.3 Examining user details
The System Administrator sets up the system users in Clinical Mode. When the System
Administrator adds a new user, they set up the user account for Service Mode or Clinical Mode.
If it is necessary for a Service User to use the Administrator functions in Clinical Mode, they must
have a different user name and password for Clinical Mode. The System Administrator sets the
user permissions for each user for some of the functions in Integrity™. If a user without user
permissions tries to use a function, a dialog box shows that they do not have the necessary user
permissions.
Elekta recommends that only the system administrator has the user permission to use this
function.

5.3.14 Description of the IntelliMax Connect sessions
If you start an IntelliMax Connect session, you must make sure that you stop the session. The
IntelliMax Connect icon appears in the status indicator area of the system. The icon stays in view,
after you log off the system, until the session is terminated.
During an active IntelliMax Connect session, the Elekta IntelliMax® support user can control the
mouse pointer, and the data input to the treatment control system. Elekta IntelliMax® support
users cannot start irradiation or patient treatment.
When the IntelliMax Connect session is active, the IntelliMax Connect dialog box shows Service
status: Active. The IntelliMax Connect icon appears in the system status indicator area.
Figure 5.15 Active IntelliMax Connect icon
When the IntelliMax Connect session is not active, the IntelliMax Connect dialog box shows
Service status: Inactive. The IntelliMax Connect icon does not appear in the system status
indicator area.
Note: An Elekta IntelliMax® support user can look at, and get access to, patient information during an
IntelliMax Connect session. It is the responsibility of the hospital-based Operator to use all
applicable local procedures to keep patient confidentiality. After an IntelliMax Connect session,
the Elekta IntelliMax® support user must erase all files transferred during the session.

6.3.12.4 Description of the units of measure used on the Dynamic Delivery Log File
Viewer window
Most of the data parameters are in known units, for example centimeters or degrees, but the leaf
and diaphragm data parameters are in internal units. The formulae that follow change the leaf
data values into known units.
To change a leaf position parameter to known units at isocenter (X-ray):
X-ray = position parameter × leaf scaling value
The leaf scale value is: Diso ÷ Dl
Where:
Diso = distance from target to isocenter, which is a nominal value of 1000.0 mm.
Dl = distance from target to leaf tip, which is a nominal value of 349.3 mm.
The leaf scale value is therefore: 1000 ÷ 349.3 = 2.863
For a position of 6 this gives:
X-ray = 6 × 0.01 × 2.863 = 0.17178 mm
To change a diaphragm position parameter to known units at isocenter (X-ray):
X-ray = position parameter × diaphragm scaling value
The diaphragm scaling value is: Diso ÷ Dd
Where:
Diso = distance from target to isocenter, which is a nominal value of 1000.0 mm
Dd = distance from target to diaphragm tip, which is a nominal value of 467.0 mm
The diaphragm scale value is therefore: 1000 ÷ 467.0 = 2.141
For a position of 46 this gives:
X-ray = 46 × 0.01 × 2.141 = 0.98486mm.
Note: Use the scaling factors, to convert the values in leaf bank level.

6.3.16 Description and operation of the dose rate parameter in Service
Mode
The dose rate parameter is part of the radiation data set for the linear accelerator. The dose rate
parameter identifies the number of MU delivered for each minute during radiation, at the
isocenter in usual conditions.
In SDR mode, the TCS sets the PRF to give a dose rate that is nearest to the prescribed dose rate,
but not more than the prescribed dose rate. For example, if the prescribed dose rate is 400, and
the maximum dose rate is 430, the TCS selects a PRF of 200 to give a dose rate of 215. If you do
not send a dose rate to the TCS from the TPS, the system delivers the radiation at the maximum
dose rate.

6.5.2 Calibrating the movement speeds
The TCS uses the maximum velocity and the ICD for each movement to calculate the dose rate for
each step of a VMAT delivery. The default value for maximum velocity is the maximum speed of
the movement. The ICD is the distance necessary for each movement to be at its maximum
velocity. The default value of the ICD is the recommended value for that movement.
Each of the geometry parameters have a maximum velocity at which they can move. Therefore,
the TCS uses the maximum velocity and the ICD for each movement to calculate the necessary
dose rate. The TCS does this for each step of the VMAT radiation delivery. When the movement
cannot keep up with the delivery, radiation delivery pauses. When this occurs the maximum
velocity or the ICD are too high, compared to the movement. You can decrease the values as a
temporary solution until you repair the movement speed.
1 Click the Calibration button.

diaphragm calibration values. If you save the new calibration values, the previous diaphragm
calibration values are deleted. If you do not save the new calibration values, all previous
calibration values are restored.
The workflow does these tests:
1 Position of MV Detector Panel
2 Pixel Size
This test calculates the ratio of millimeters at isocenter to MV detector panel pixels. The
workflow uses the ratio to display test results in millimeters at isocenter.
3 Radiation Center
This test finds the center of rotation of the radiation beam.
4 Diaphragm Calibration
This test does the fine calibration of the diaphragms. It finds the correct position of each
diaphragm from the radiation center.

The remote viewer application (RVA) enables you to switch between different channels. For
example, display MOSAIQ® Sequencer or Integrity™ on the monitors in the treatment room or in

number 1 on the left and number 2 second from the left.
• In a grid layout of monitors, the monitors are numbered in columns from left to right
and within each column, they are numbered top to bottom.

7.5.2 Configuring the RVA with the Terminal Services Configuration Editor
The Terminal Services Configuration Editor is the tool used to configure the Remote Viewer
Application (RVA).
These are the rules that apply to the RVA settings on the CCP management computer:
• There must always be at least one non-RVA monitor so that you can access the CCP
Management Panel (CCPMP). The non-RVA monitor must be the CCPMP primary
display.
• The R&V channel must be on a non-RVA monitor.
• For a horizontal layout of the monitors, the RVA monitors must always be next to each
other and cannot have a non-RVA monitor between them.
• For a grid layout of monitors, the RVA can occupy a single monitor or two monitors. If it
occupies two monitors then the monitors must be in the same row, or the same
column.
• You cannot configure the Integrity primary monitor as hidden as it is a regulatory
requirement for it to always be visible. The Terminal Services Configuration Editor
application stops you from making this monitor hidden.
• The Integrity primary channel must be configured as Critical.
• If a channel is read-only, the mouse movement is not permitted on that monitor
displaying the read-only channel.

8.5 Troubleshooting of the Enterprise server
You can use the iLO tool for the diagnosis of possible Enterprise server issues. The iLO tool lets
you do remote monitoring and management of servers. With HPE iLO you can configure, update,
monitor, and repair remote servers. HPE servers have iLO installed.
The iLO general system information displays information such as the health summary page. This
shows the status of monitored subsystems and devices. It is a good starting point for
troubleshooting.
The event log provides a record of significant events recorded by the iLO firmware. This can prove
useful in determining the cause of faults. iLO event logs are described in the HPE iLO user guide.
For more information, refer to the HPE ProLiant Gen10 server troubleshooting guide.
8.5.1 Running iLO to do troubleshooting of the Enterprise server
You can use the iLO health summary web page to view status information about configured
subsystems and devices.
You can also view the event logs, which contain a record from the iLO firmware of the identified
events. For more information, refer to the HPE iLO user guide.
1 On the CCP Management Computer, open a browser and type https://
192.168.240.250.
2 Log on with the default username and password.
8.5.2 Noise from the Enterprise server
The Enterprise Server (ES) can make sounds which you can easily hear as it starts up. You cannot
usually hear it after it has fully started.
It is not usually necessary to restart the ES.
You must do the troubleshooting if the ES gives loud sounds during its normal operation.
For more information, refer to the HPE ProLiant Gen10 server Troubleshooting guide. Start at the
Fan and thermal issues section.

Shutting down the system to do maintenance tasks
9.1 Shutting down the system to do maintenance tasks
You must shut down the applicable parts of the system before you do maintenance tasks. This is
the usual procedure to shut down the CCP and its related equipment.
1 In the CCP Management Panel, shut down the TRM computer.
2 In Integrity, follow the procedure to switch off Integrity.
Note: You must put Integrity into Standby mode and then click Power Off.
3 In IntelliMax, shut down IntelliMax.
4 In the CCP Management Panel, shut down the CCP Management Computer (CCPMC).
5 Switch off the Enterprise Server (ES).
a Press the POWER button of the ES one time.
b Make sure that the Power LED of the ES changes to an amber color after a short period
of time.
6 Switch off the real-time controller (RTC).
a Press the POWER button of the RTC.
b Make sure that the green Power LED goes off.
7 Switch off the Network-attached storage (NAS).
a Press the POWER button until you hear a 'beep' after approximately two seconds.
b When you hear the 'beep', immediately release the POWER button.
This prevents a 'hard' switch off.
8 Switch off the NMaS.
a On the Network Management and Security (NMaS), press the POWER button one time
and immediately release it.
9 If applicable, shut down the independent R&V computer.
10 Do a check that all the rack devices are fully switched off.
11 Shut down the UPS.
a Press the POWER button of the UPS for some time.
b When you hear a 'beep' sound, release the POWER button of the UPS.
12 Disconnect the power supply cable from the rear panel of the CCP cabinet.

the Enterprise Server (ES).

Gen10 Server Maintenance and Service guide.

2 With the supplied key, unlock the CCP cabinet door.
3 Open the CCP cabinet door more than 90° to the CCP cabinet.
You can then get access to the latch on the inner edge of the door.
4 Carefully move the latch down.
The door will slide out at the upper end.
5 Lift the door and put it on the side of the CCP cabinet.
Note: The ground earth cable continues to be attached.
6 At the rear of the CC cabinet, open the lower patch panel to get access to the cables.
7 Remove these cables from the rear of the ES:
– Ethernet cable connector in purple network port 34
– Ethernet cable connector in green network port 12
– Ethernet cable connector in red network port 6
– Ethernet cable connector in orange network port 4
– Server 1 AC (2)
– Server 1 AC (1).
8 Hold the two sides of the ES, and carefully pull it out of the CCP cabinet.
The full depth of the ES moves out of the CCP cabinet on rollers.
9 To remove the ES fully from the CCP cabinet, carefully push down on the buttons on the rails
and, with a second approved person, lift the ES out of the rails.
Note: Two persons are necessary to lift the ES out of the rails.

9.11 Network-attached storage (NAS) in the CCP cabinet
9.11.1 Removing the NAS of the CCP cabinet
You can get access to the Network-attached storage (NAS) from the front of the CCP cabinet.
1 With the supplied key, unlock the CCP cabinet door.
2 Shut down the NAS. Press the POWER button until you hear a 'beep' after approximately two
seconds. When you hear the 'beep', immediately release the POWER button to prevent a
'hard' switch off.
3 Make sure that all the NAS LEDs are off.
4 Open the CCP cabinet door more than 90° to the CCP cabinet.
You can then get access to the latch on the inner edge of the door.
5 Carefully move the latch down.
The door will slide out at the upper end.
6 Lift the door and put it on the side of the CCP cabinet.
Note: The ground earth cable continues to be attached.
7 At the rear of the CCP, open the lower patch panel to get access to the cables.
8 At the rear connector panel of the NAS, remove the Ethernet cables and power supply
cables.
9 Remove the two screws from the front panel of the NAS.
10 Hold the two sides of the NAS, and carefully pull it out of the CCP cabinet.
9.11.2 Installing the NAS of the CCP cabinet
You can get access to the Network-attached storage (NAS) from the front of the CCP cabinet.
1 If necessary, use the supplied key to unlock the CCP cabinet door.
2 At the rear of the CCP, open the lower patch panel to get access to the cables.
3 Carefully push the NAS into its position in the CCP cabinet.
4 At the rear connector panel of the NAS, connect the Ethernet cables and power supply
cables.
– Ethernet cable connector in purple network port 34
– Ethernet cable connector in green network port 12
– Ethernet cable connector in red network port 6
– Ethernet cable connector in orange network port 4
– Server 1 AC (2)
– Server 1 AC (1).
5 Press the POWER button on the front panel of the NAS. Make sure that it starts.
6 Lift the door and put its lower latch into its hole in the CCP base.
7 Make sure that the ground earth cable continues to be attached to the door
8 Lower the upper latch and put it in the hole in the CCP ceiling panel to hold the door latch.

9.12 Network switch
9.12.1 Removing the network switch from the CCP cabinet
The network switch is at the rear of the CCP cabinet, between the Network-attached storage
(NAS) and the Network Management and Security (NMaS) cabinets.
1 Make sure that the CCP cabinet is not energized.
2 Undo the thumb screws of the rear bottom service hatch cover.
3 Remove the cross-head screw of the rear bottom service hatch cover.
4 Open the rear bottom service hatch cover.
5 Disconnect the electrical supply cable from the rear panel of the network switch.
6 At the front panel of the network switch, record the network cable connectors and
disconnect them.
7 Undo the four screws on the front panel of the network switch.
8 Carefully remove the network switch from the CCP cabinet.
9.12.2 Installing the network switch in the CCP cabinet
The network switch is at the rear of the CCP cabinet, between the Network-attached storage
(NAS) and the Network Management and Security (NMaS) cabinets.
1 Make sure that the CCP cabinet is not energized.
2 Carefully install the network switch in its correct position in the CCP cabinet.
3 Tighten the four screws on the front panel of the network switch.
4 At the front panel of the network switch, connect the network cable connectors.
5 If necessary, open the rear bottom service hatch cover.
6 Connect the electrical supply cable at the rear panel of the network switch.
7 Close the rear bottom service hatch cover.
8 Close the thumb screws of the rear bottom service hatch.
9 Tighten the cross-head screw of the rear bottom service hatch.
10 Close and lock the front door of the CCP cabinet.

5 Close and lock the CCP cabinet.

10.1 Description of where to find the planned maintenance
information
The Planned Maintenance (PM) checks keep the system at the correct conditions for operation.
PM checks extend the time interval that the equipment can operate without corrective
maintenance.
Refer to the applicable Instructions for Use - Clinical Mode for an overview of the planned
maintenance tasks for the Elekta Medical Linear Accelerator (EMLA). Full instructions on how to
do the planned maintenance of the equipment is in the EMLA Planned Maintenance Manual.
WARNING 10.1
Do not work on the linear accelerator before you know the date and time of when the system
restart is scheduled. This is to make sure that the equipment will not become live, with high
voltages, while you are in the equipment. If you ignore this warning, you can cause fatal injury.
